cors_misconfiguration.summary: Casdoor CORS misconfiguration permits cross-origin actions in signed-in context
cors_misconfiguration.description: GitHub Security Lab reported a CORS misconfiguration in Casdoor. The vulnerable CORS filter accepted attacker-controlled Origin values that matched unsafe prefixes and then reflected that origin through Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also enabling Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. The primary advisory shows the response header logic and explains that a malicious cross-origin website could make requests as the current signed-in user. This source is used only to define inert reflected-Origin versus trusted-Origin response fixtures; no live request is sent.

ldap_injection.summary: Redash LDAP authentication filter can be altered by unauthenticated user input
ldap_injection.description: GitHub Security Lab reported LDAP injection in Redash authentication. User-controlled identity input was formatted into an LDAP search filter, allowing crafted input to alter directory filter semantics and authentication/search behavior. The primary advisory includes the vulnerable auth_ldap_user flow and an example injected LDAP filter. This source is translated only into inert raw LDAP query/error/control fixtures; no live directory request is executed.

server_side_template_injection.summary: Apache OFBiz FreeMarker rendering accepts untrusted server-side template expressions
server_side_template_injection.description: GitHub Security Lab reported Server-Side Template Injection in Apache OFBiz. Untrusted request data reached a FreeMarker macro/template rendering path, allowing injected template expressions to be evaluated server-side. The primary advisory documents the request parameter flow into renderLookupField and the resulting server template execution condition. This source is converted only into an inert template-render/error fixture and secure controls; no expression is executed by the benchmark collector.

note: Primary GitHub Security Lab research advisories used only where the fully unseen GitHub Reviewed Advisory pool had no remaining family source after excluding all prior v2 candidate roots. No detector scoring was used to select these sources.
